広場ダンスに象棋、書道、古箏、バドミントン、山歩き、釣り、ドラマ、マーダーミステ: From square dancing and Chinese chess to calligraphy, the guzheng, badminton, hiking, fishing, TV dramas, murder mystery games, photography and balcony gardening. Conversations for connecting with people in China through hobbies.
杭州に来て一か月の山本さん。夕食のあと団地の中を散歩していると、広場で大勢の人が: Shota Yamamoto has been in Hangzhou for a month. Out for a walk around his housing complex after dinner, he finds a crowd of people dancing to music in the square. He stops to watch, and the woman dancing at the front comes over with a smile.
広場ダンスのチームのリーダー、六十歳前後。明るく世話好き: Leader of the square-dancing group, around sixty. Cheerful and loves looking after people

同じ団地に住む年配の女性と、引っ越してきたばかりの若い男性。中国では年上の女性を: An older woman and a young man who has just moved into the same housing complex. In China, older women are called 「阿姨」, and people speak warmly even when meeting for the first time. Neighbors in a housing complex are usually quite close, so don't hold back too much: respond with a smile.
お兄さん、さっきからずっと見てるわね。一緒に踊らない？: Young man, you've been watching for ages. Why not dance with us?

でも下手だから、ついていけないんじゃないかな。: But I'm a bad dancer. What if I can't keep up?

あ、そんなに難しくなさそうです。皆さん毎日ここで踊ってるんですか。: Oh, it doesn't seem too hard. Do you all dance here every day?
そう、雨の日以外は毎晩七時から八時半まで。: Yes. Every evening from seven to eight thirty, except when it rains.

毎日一時間半ですか。けっこうな運動量ですね。: An hour and a half every day? That's quite a workout.
そうよ。私は五年踊ってるけど、前は腰が悪かったのに、今は全然平気。: That's right. I've been dancing for five years. My back used to be bad, but now I have no problems at all.

「广场舞」は、団地の広場や公園で、音楽に合わせて大勢で踊る中国ならではの光景です: 「广场舞」 (square dancing), where large groups dance to music in housing-complex squares and parks, is a uniquely Chinese sight. Most dancers are women from their fifties to their seventies, and it's a way to stay healthy and socialize. The music ranges from pop songs to folk songs, and some teams dance with fans or scarves. Disputes with neighbors over the volume sometimes make the news, and these days more groups set fixed hours or keep the music quieter. People often invite you just for watching, so feel free to join in.
